title: The boss fight's next round, the final review's fixes: a tank stopped behind a rock was eaten through it, the fear was invisible and misdescribed (it flees 74.5 % of a fight, not three or five times), and a reset could stand an obstacle up inside the creature or the tank
context: The final whole-round review of the next round (2026-10-08-boss-fight-next-round-landed, corrected by -jitter-corrected) found three things. (1) CRITICAL: the lab set `motion.targetHeld` from the tank's movement before the routing replaced the creature's target with a waypoint. The kit captures whatever `motion.target` is (feeding.js: within 0.075 native of the torso for 0.1 s while `canCapture = active && !targetHeld`), and a waypoint is always that close (about 0.3 rad ahead on the clearance circle, within about 12.5 m of the torso when the creature is near a rock), so a tank that merely stopped behind a rock was eaten through it: the lab moved the tank to the prey position (the waypoint) and the round went LOST 'caught'. (2) The fear: a node simulation showed the creature fleeing 73.8 % and stunned 4.9 % of a 31 s fight while `frights` read 1, because frights counts fresh episodes and SOL's beam sits 10 m past the front edge (radius 8 plus reach 8), so it is in reach for 6 s of every 8 s. The landing entry's playtest point (2) spoke of how often the fright runs (3 to 5 frights and 3 to 4 stuns), which is the wrong measure. (3) `setFight` called `arena.reset(false)` and turning the obstacles on showed the shapes again, so a breakable could stand up inside the creature or the tank.
outcome: Fixed in four commits on refactor-run, never pushed. (1) boss-tab.js: after the routing block, `if (routed || fr.mode === 'flee') m.targetHeld = true` (targetHeld only gates the capture, behavior.js; pursuit is unaffected): a waypoint or a flee point is never prey. The handle gained `parkBehind(id, off)` (the tank on the far side of a shape, 8 m off its face, not held) and `--boss-walls` a shield step: a fresh round, the fight off, the tank parked 8 m behind r1, 15 s of lab clock, a per-frame sampler. RED on the old code: captured at 9.65 s with the creature 30.1 m from the tank, the tank moved 21.2 m to the waypoint. GREEN: not captured in 15 s, the closest approach 28.5 m, the creature still 18 m from r1's centre (it has not got round the rock by 15 s). (2) The fear keeps the round's seconds (src/labs/boss/fear.js, restarted with the round); the readout shows the live fear mode and the share of the round fleeing and stunned; the handle's fight() exposes `fleeShare` and `stunShare`; the survival run logs both. MEASURED in the survival run (health 180, the dodging circle): KILLED at 31.87 s, 3 frights, 3 stuns, fleeing 74.5 % and stunned 4.7 % of the fight, taken 0 (the earlier 31.03 s and 31.86 s; the fix to the capture did not move it). So the creature spends three quarters of the fight running from the beam's footprint and about one twentieth stunned. OWNER'S PLAYTEST POINT, restated: the fright's feel is not how often it runs but whether a creature that flees for three quarters of the fight reads as afraid of SOL or as a boss that never turns on the tank; SOL's weight 2, its 0.8 s after-time, the 20 m flee and the 8 m reach are the knobs (fightTune.fear in the panel), and a stun of 1.5 s every 20 s is small beside it. (3) The in-place reset (`arena.reset(false)`) revives only the shapes whose footprint is clear of the creature (its centre and its extent, 30 m) and the tank (the hull), and the obstacles switch coming on takes down (`arena.settle()`) the standing shapes on them; the rest come back at the next round (src/domain/boss-arena.js `restoreClear`, `withdrawFrom`, node tests). Minors: the fear's header names the lab's monotonic clock as `now` and why (clearFear keeps lastDisturb; the fight's clock restarts each round); the readout reads `ms/step` and `nuke in off` with the MK-9 switch off; the stale gunship comments name the four guns and the obstacles that stay with the fight off; two overlapping burns counted a plan's hit again each time they alternated (`state.burning` held one plan): `state.burnt` is the set of plans counted, with a node test (6 alternating burns of two plans are 2 hits; 6 before). The other browser numbers of the final run: the standing body killed at 28.03 s, the circling step half by the rate (3.99 hp/s against 3.75), the walls 0.5733 ms a frame, jitter 0.0740 m a frame, 9 moves over 1.5 m. AS BUILT, for the owner's call: the survival run's dodge is a perfect-knowledge player (it reads the plan's point from the rules) widening to max(75 m, the ring point's distance from the centre + 55 m + the hull + 3 m), about 85 to 90 m, so 31.87 s is the kill time of a player who always sees the ring; and the nuke's lead (the aim leads the creature's velocity by `lead` of the time to landing) can put its point up to about 25 m off the centre, possibly in front of a charging creature. Whether the lead should shrink is the owner's call after the playtest. The other judgement points of the landing entry (the nuke's 55 m ring against the tank, the push-out's look, the 3 m flip across a wall, the dither at 6 to 14 m behind a wall) stand.
alternatives: Hold the target in the kit (src/fx/nih-dairia/feeding.js): rejected, the port is not modified; the lab sets targetHeld.
Count a stopped tank as held only while routed, but not while fleeing: rejected, a flee point is also never the tank, and the same capture of a point would move the tank to it.
Revive every obstacle in place and rely on the push-out and the blocker: rejected, the push-out moves the body's nodes at once and the tank's blocker shoves it by the shape's depth; it pops.
Edit the landing entries: rejected, validated entries are immutable; this entry supersedes the jitter-corrected one.
evidence: scripts/browser-lock.sh node scripts/browser-test.mjs --boss-walls from a snapshot of the old code: BOSS-WALLS shield captured at 9.65 s, 30.1 m from the tank, the tank moved 21.2 m (assertion: the creature ate the tank through r1); with the fix: not captured, PASS
